note: #def names are their own bucket, never folded into `sets` — the two directives differ in semantics, so a consumer that lints one must be able to tell them apart. Arrays are order-normalized. Tagged ts+py because the PHP runner does not assert `defs` yet; it can drop the tag once it does (its Parser already returns them).

The gap after #include is the spelled-out ASCII class: space, tab, LF, CR, FF, VT. An NBSP (the escaped U+00A0 here) is not part of it, so this line is plain text, not an include. No engine may reach for its dialect's whitespace shorthand: PHP's u modifier turns on PCRE2_UCP, whose shorthand matches NBSP and all of Zs — the engines measurably disagreed on this exact template (spintax-js#55) until the class was spelled out on the PHP side too. This fixture is what keeps it one set.
Every member of the ASCII class counts, including the two nobody types — this gap is an escaped U+000B vertical tab.

The gap here is an escaped U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR: it ends a line for the anchors but is NOT gap whitespace, so this line is plain text. The trap this guards: a port that normalizes terminators to LF before scanning folds the separator into the LF the gap class itself contains, and one engine returns two answers for the same line — the Python engine's extract/validate did exactly that while its renderer got it right (fixed alongside spintax-js#55).

The gap here is an escaped U+0085 NEL, which is in PCRE2's UCP whitespace but is neither in the contract's class nor an ECMAScript line terminator — the sharpest single character for pinning that the gap is a spelled-out set, not any dialect's shorthand.

The character after the closing quote is an escaped U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR. It is not in the whitespace class, but it IS a line end for the multiline anchors, so the trailing run stops in front of it and the include matches. PCRE's /m anchors break on LF only — the other half of the same question, spelled out as lookarounds on the PHP side.
The class question on the other side of the target: the character after the closing quote is an escaped U+00A0 NBSP — not trailing whitespace, so no line end is reachable and the line is plain text.

A #set whose name is not ASCII defines nothing and its reference refers to nothing — the whole line is text (#56). The verdict and render halves are pinned by validate/set-nonascii-name-is-malformed and render/set-name-nonascii-is-not-a-directive.
The anchor half on the directive grammar: a bare \r ends a line, so the #set after it is a directive and defines its name (#56).

The conditional-ref collector's name tail is ASCII, mirroring the renderer's name rule: {?xя?y} is not a conditional to any renderer in the family, so it must not contribute a phantom ref either. PHP's validator collected 'xя' via \w under UCP while its own Conditionals::NAME_RE (spelled-out ASCII) refused it (#56).

A bare escaped U+000D CR ends a line for the anchors (ECMAScript's set: LF, CR, U+2028, U+2029), so the directive after it starts a line and matches. PCRE's /m breaks on LF alone — the anchor half in the direction the wide-whitespace engines used to REJECT.
